sections.heading: 1. Who we are
paragraphs: OpsClear is operated by [[LEGAL_ENTITY_NAME]] ([[LEGAL_ENTITY_ADDRESS]], registration number [[REGISTRATION_NUMBER]], tax number [[TAX_NUMBER]]), called "we" or "us" below. By creating an account or using OpsClear you agree to these terms. If you use OpsClear for a business, you confirm that you can accept these terms on its behalf.

sections.heading: 2. The service
paragraphs: OpsClear is a web application for tracking operational work: jobs, their statuses, blockages, notes and approvals. Features depend on the plan and add-ons your organisation subscribes to.

sections.heading: 3. Accounts and organisations
paragraphs: You need an account, and a verified email address, to use OpsClear. Keep your password secret and tell us if you think your account was misused. One person can belong to one organisation. The person who creates an organisation is its owner and is responsible for the people they invite and for what they do in it.

sections.heading: 4. Acceptable use
paragraphs: You agree not to:
items: break the law or use OpsClear to store or share unlawful content
try to access other organisations' data, or to disrupt, probe or overload the service
share your account in a way that avoids paying for more seats or add-ons
resell or white-label the service without our written permission

sections.heading: 5. Subscriptions and billing
paragraphs: Paid plans are billed in advance for each billing period (monthly or yearly) and renew automatically until cancelled. Prices are shown at checkout.

Payments are handled by Paddle, which is the merchant of record for your purchase. Paddle sells the subscription to you, collects the payment and any taxes, and issues the invoice. Paddle's buyer terms apply to the purchase, in addition to these terms.

sections.heading: 6. Free trial
paragraphs: New organisations may get a free trial of 7 days. When the trial ends, access requires a paid subscription.

sections.heading: 7. Cancellation and refunds
paragraphs: You can cancel at any time from your organisation's billing settings. Cancelling stops the next renewal, and access continues until the end of the period you paid for. Refunds are described in our Refund policy.

sections.heading: 8. Lock-out after the trial or non-payment
paragraphs: When the trial ends without a subscription, or a payment fails and isn't fixed, the organisation is locked: members can no longer use the app. Data is kept for a limited time so you can resubscribe and carry on, and may be deleted after that.

sections.heading: 9. Your data
paragraphs: You own the content you put into OpsClear (jobs, notes and so on). You give us the right to store and process it only to provide the service to you. How we handle personal data is described in the Privacy Policy.

sections.heading: 10. Availability
paragraphs: We work to keep OpsClear running, but we don't promise uninterrupted or error-free service and there is no service level agreement. We may change the service, and do maintenance.

sections.heading: 11. Liability
paragraphs: OpsClear is provided "as is". To the extent the law allows, we aren't liable for indirect or consequential loss, lost profit or lost data, and our total liability for any claim is limited to the amount you paid us in the 12 months before the claim.
Nothing in these terms limits liability that can't be limited by law, or your rights as a consumer where they apply.

sections.heading: 12. Termination
paragraphs: You can stop using OpsClear at any time. We may suspend or end an account that breaks these terms, after warning you where that is reasonable.

sections.heading: 13. Governing law
paragraphs: These terms are governed by the laws of [[GOVERNING_LAW_COUNTRY]], and the courts there decide disputes, without removing any consumer protection that applies to you by law.

sections.heading: 14. Changes to these terms
paragraphs: We may update these terms. For material changes we will tell you by email or in the app before they apply. Continuing to use OpsClear after that means you accept them.

sections.heading: 15. Contact
paragraphs: Questions about these terms: [[SUPPORT_EMAIL]].

sections.heading: 1. Who is responsible
paragraphs: The data controller is [[LEGAL_ENTITY_NAME]], [[LEGAL_ENTITY_ADDRESS]] (registration number [[REGISTRATION_NUMBER]]). Contact for privacy questions: [[SUPPORT_EMAIL]]. For the content your organisation puts into jobs and notes, your organisation is the controller and we act as its processor.

sections.heading: 2. What we collect
paragraphs: We process:
items: Account data: your name and email address, and your sign-in, handled through our login service (Keycloak)
Content: what you and your colleagues put into jobs, notes, approvals and settings
Technical data: server logs such as IP address, browser, time and requested page, used for security and troubleshooting
Billing data: held by Paddle, our payment provider and merchant of record. We receive the subscription status and invoice details, not your card number

sections.heading: 3. Why, and on what legal basis
paragraphs: To provide the service you signed up for (performing our contract with you): accounts, jobs, notifications, billing status.
To keep the service secure and working (our legitimate interest): logs, abuse prevention, fixing errors.
To meet legal obligations such as tax and accounting records.

sections.heading: 4. Who we share it with
paragraphs: We use these sub-processors:
items: [[SMTP_PROVIDER]]: sending emails such as verification and invitations

sections.heading: 5. How long we keep it
paragraphs: We keep account and content data while your organisation has an account. After an organisation is deleted or lapses, we delete its data within [[RETENTION_PERIOD]], except what the law requires us to keep, such as invoices. Logs are kept for a short period.

sections.heading: 6. Your rights
paragraphs: Under the GDPR (and Serbia's data protection law) you can ask for access to your data, correction, deletion, a copy in a portable format, restriction or objection to processing. For now, send these requests by email to [[SUPPORT_EMAIL]] and we will answer within one month. You can also complain to your data protection authority.

sections.heading: 7. Cookies
paragraphs: OpsClear uses only the cookies and browser storage needed to sign you in and remember your language and theme. We don't use advertising or tracking cookies. If that changes, we will update this policy and ask for consent where required.

sections.heading: 8. Changes and contact
paragraphs: We will update this policy if what we do changes, and tell you about material changes. Questions: [[SUPPORT_EMAIL]].

sections.heading: 1. Cancel anytime
paragraphs: You can cancel your subscription at any time from your organisation's billing settings. Cancelling stops the next renewal. Access continues until the end of the period you have already paid for.

sections.heading: 2. No refunds for paid periods
paragraphs: Except where required by law or by our reseller's terms, we don't refund a billing period that has already been paid, whether or not you used the service during it.

sections.heading: 3. Try before you pay
paragraphs: Every new organisation can use a 7-day free trial, which is the way to find out whether OpsClear fits before you pay.

sections.heading: 4. Paddle and your legal rights
paragraphs: Paddle is the merchant of record for your purchase. Its buyer terms may give you rights, such as a statutory withdrawal period in some regions, and Paddle may grant a refund in line with them. Nothing in this policy limits rights you have by law.

sections.heading: 5. Contact
paragraphs: Billing questions: [[SUPPORT_EMAIL]].
